skills.name: Money: functions and the limits of barter

note.text: Money is an asset broadly accepted for payment in its community. As a medium of exchange it separates selling from buying, reducing the need to find someone who simultaneously wants what the seller offers. As a unit of account it expresses comparable prices. As a store of value it carries purchasing ability over time, though inflation can erode that ability. Money can also express deferred payments. A useful object or a payment instruction is not automatically money.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish money’s functions and explain how a medium of exchange reduces a barter obstacle. Builds on: Form Four trade, production and exchange. Leads to: qualities of money, money demand and purchasing power.

sections.heading: Understand the economics
sections.text: Money is an asset broadly accepted for payment in its community. As a medium of exchange it separates selling from buying, reducing the need to find someone who simultaneously wants what the seller offers. As a unit of account it expresses comparable prices. As a store of value it carries purchasing ability over time, though inflation can erode that ability. Money can also express deferred payments. A useful object or a payment instruction is not automatically money.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: In a fictional Bamenda market, a notebook seller wants vegetables but the vegetable seller does not want notebooks. An accepted currency can separate the exchanges. Prices quoted in CFA francs also give a common accounting unit. Holding a cash balance for later does not guarantee its future purchasing power.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the particular obstacle or function in the case. Separate the thing being paid from an instruction to transfer it. Do not confuse money with all wealth or assume every valuable item is readily accepted in payment.

standard of deferred payment: The real burden can change with the price level.

pick.q: Why can accepted currency help when the vegetable seller does not want notebooks?
pick.r: It separates the sale from the later purchase.
w: It makes all goods equally priced.
It eliminates every production cost.
It guarantees no price changes.
e: A common medium does not equalise prices.
Exchange does not remove production costs.
Money does not guarantee stable prices.
pick.y: The sellers no longer need matching immediate wants.

pick.q: A pupil compares folder and notebook prices in CFA francs. Which function is central?
pick.r: Unit of account.
w: Store of value only.
Physical durability.
An instruction to transfer a deposit.
e: The case is a price comparison, not retaining balances.
Durability is a quality, not this comparison function.
No payment instruction is described.
pick.y: The common unit permits comparison.

pick.q: A seller keeps a balance for next week. What qualification is needed?
pick.r: Its later purchasing power may change.
w: It becomes worthless by definition overnight.
It must buy exactly the same basket forever.
It proves the seller owns no other wealth.
e: A possibility of change is not inevitable worthlessness.
Price changes can alter the basket.
A money balance says nothing complete about other assets.
pick.y: Store of value is not a guarantee of constant real value.

pick.q: Which distinction is correct?
pick.r: A cheque instructs payment from a deposit; it is not identical to the deposit balance.
w: A cheque is necessarily central-bank cash.
Every valuable machine is immediately money.
A price label is itself a paid debt.
e: A cheque is a payment instrument.
Valuable wealth need not be broadly accepted in payment.
A label states a price rather than paying it.
pick.y: Separate money, wealth and payment instructions.
